heading: What he thinks about.
intro: Nahim writes most weeks on LinkedIn, mostly about youth work, leadership and looking after yourself. A few recurring themes:

items.title: Presence, not perfection
items.excerpt: In his first week as a youth worker he thought he needed all the answers. He didn’t. Trust is built in ordinary moments: showing up, remembering names, keeping promises. Young people won’t remember every activity. They’ll remember how you made them feel.

items.title: Nobody is hard to reach
items.excerpt: The phrase gets pinned on young people. In Nahim’s experience it usually describes the institution: hard to reach, and almost impossible to trust.
items.source: Talk at BLOC, Queen Mary University of London

items.title: Words as fuel
items.excerpt: On the teacher who told him he’d never amount to anything, and the choice every person has about what to do with the words other people give them.

items.title: Don’t neglect yourself while pouring into others
items.excerpt: Looking after yourself isn’t selfish. For a youth worker it’s part of the job. Nahim on the weight he lost, and the stress and habits that went with it.
